THO-NW.label: Northwest Upland
THO-NW.headline: Gemini Field Agronomy Dossier: THO-NW (Northwest Upland)
THO-NW.executive_summary: Parcel THO-NW (Northwest Upland) sits on deep Keith silt loam tableland at 39.46° N, -101.12° W. The 10-year MODIS record detects a peak NDVI of 0.59 during wheat heading, followed by a critical 4-month bare window (July–October). Under 30–50 mph spring winds, pulverized fallow topsoil in this parcel is classified as a 'Severe Wind Detachment Zone'. Replacing open summer fallow with Wheat w/ Legume Cover maintains soil armor and eliminates midsummer evaporative burn-off.
THO-NW.detailed_agronomy:
• Recommended Strategy: **Wheat w/ Legume Cover**
• Heat & Moisture Buffer: NASA POWER records 33.0 days/yr ≥ 35°C; root-zone wetness index is 0.373.
• Actionable Advice: Check subsoil moisture to 4 feet in late May. If profile is moist, plant sorghum or cover mix to shield soil before July heat.

FIN-NW.label: Northwest Upland
FIN-NW.headline: Gemini Field Agronomy Dossier: FIN-NW (Northwest Upland)
FIN-NW.executive_summary: Parcel FIN-NW (Northwest Upland) at 38.04° N, -100.94° W is within the intensive center-pivot irrigation belt of Finney County. NASA satellite thermal observations reveal that adjacent bare ground heats to 125°F, driving higher evaporative demand across center pivots during 43.0 annual heat days (≥35°C). Classified as a 'High Atmospheric Heat Stress', continued continuous corn will accelerate local Ogallala drawdown.
FIN-NW.detailed_agronomy:
• Recommended Strategy: **Corn–Soybean**
• Water Conservation Impact: Adopting Corn–Soybean cuts seasonal pumping by ~6.8 inches/acre, saving over 23 million gallons of groundwater per pivot.
• Actionable Advice: Split circle nozzles between corn and grain sorghum to stagger peak pumping windows and comply with GMD 3 LEMA allocations.
